target_customer: Product managers, growth and engineering teams at software companies that pay annual subscriptions for product analytics
problem: Teams had to decide in advance which events to track and write code for each one, so questions about past behavior often could not be answered.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced on data volume, with product-led growth
product_category: Product analytics with automatic event capture

founders.name: Matin Movassate
founders.background_notes: Reportedly conceived the idea while at Facebook; education sources conflict (MIT vs Stanford) across secondary pages.

founders.name: Ravi Parikh
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder in secondary sources; YC page lists only Movassate.

competitors.name: Mixpanel
competitors.what: Event-based product analytics requiring events to be defined and instrumented up front
competitors.traction_then: Dominant model of the time per a retrospective origin story

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing all clicks and page views through one snippet and letting users define events retroactively required a storage and query design that was hard for a small team but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Historical data stored in the product created some lock in, but automatic capture could be copied by rivals and later was.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors later added autocapture, and Heap was acquired by Contentsquare in 2023 for an undisclosed sum.

market_need_then: Teams using event-first tools had to plan tracking in advance; the 2013 seed round and later growth show demand for a no-code capture approach.

branding.domain_note: Early blog at heapanalytics.com, later heap.io.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, outcome focused, short punchy headlines

branding.brand_signature: Retroactive analysis, nicknamed time travel by users

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in product analytics with a clear one idea pitch, but little evidence of community, merch or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Heap differentiated from event-first tools like Mixpanel through automatic capture and retroactive analysis, spread through product-led growth, and raised about 205 million dollars across rounds through 2021. As rivals matched autocapture it was acquired by Contentsquare in late 2023 for an undisclosed amount, described as the buyer's largest deal.
notes: Series A 2016 investors from a search summary of a Global Venturing article; Series D 2021 lead differs between ZoomInfo (Menlo) and Preqin (Sixth Street) and amount is from a single aggregator, so treat as unverified; seed amount of 2 million from one blog only. Total raised reported as 95.2 million after Series C and 214.1 million by ZoomInfo. Co-founder Ravi Parikh is not on the YC page. Acquisition price undisclosed.
